statusDetail: Atomic coverage complete across 58 checks and six representative public paths. Purchase was not irreversibly submitted; checkout entry and sign-in were inspected.

page.framework: Amazon server-rendered templates with client enhancement
page.notes: Large UK commerce site. Coverage includes home, search, product, basket, sign-in entry and error recovery. Account settings, seller tools, Prime Video, order history and post-auth checkout were not covered because they are distinct authenticated/product surfaces and no credentials were provided.

paths.description: Homepage and first-visit consent experience, representing discovery and global chrome.
Search/listing archetype for the primary product-discovery journey.
Product-detail archetype, pricing, availability, media, and add-to-basket controls.
Basket/checkout entry state and recovery from an empty basket.
Authentication entry reached from basket, inspected for labels, autocomplete and passkey/WebAuthn support.
Invalid product URL representing an HTTP/application error recovery state.

findings.summary: The experience ignores the user’s dark colour preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot remains the same white/light catalogue as the normal capture; DOM computed styles report color-scheme: normal and product CSS contains no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven surface/text tokens using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Loading shimmer motion continues under reduced-motion.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe reports 34 running _aXZlL_loadingShimmer animations, each 1500 ms, while matchMedia confirms prefers-reduced-motion: reduce; product CSS has no matching media rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable or replace non-essential shimmer animations inside prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

findings.summary: No explicit high-contrast or forced-colours adaptation is present.
findings.evidence: Product CSS contains no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rules; controls rely heavily on custom sprite colours. Lighthouse found no ordinary text contrast failure, so this is a preference-support gap rather than a general contrast failure.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast adaptations for essential custom controls and focus indicators.

findings.summary: State changes do not use modern declarative transition primitives.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no view-transition CSS or scroll animation timeline; the add-to-basket screencast produced only two abrupt state frames.
findings.suggestedFix: Use View Transitions for meaningful state changes and CSS animation timelines for genuinely scroll-linked effects, with reduced-motion fallbacks.

findings.summary: Global navigation does not use scroll-state or anchor positioning for contextual chrome.
findings.evidence: Homepage/product CSS has no @container scroll-state, anchor-name, position-anchor, or position-try signals despite numerous role=dialog/menu surfaces.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance sticky chrome with scroll-state queries and attach menus/tooltips with CSS anchor positioning plus fallbacks.

findings.summary: The first-visit consent panel obscures a large share of the core page.
findings.evidence: Fresh-profile homepage and product screenshots show a fixed consent form covering roughly the lower 40% of a 1000 px viewport. The overlay is dismissible and offers equal Accept/Decline controls, but content is substantially obscured.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the panel footprint, preserve equal choices, and use a semantic dismissible dialog pattern that keeps context visible.

findings.summary: Overlay infrastructure is largely custom rather than native semantic primitives.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found 25 role-dialog/aria-modal surfaces but zero dialog and zero popover elements; the consent UI is a fixed form.
findings.suggestedFix: Migrate modal flows to dialog and transient menus to popover with declarative light-dismiss.

findings.summary: Dense global chrome and horizontal card rails crowd primary content.
findings.evidence: Homepage screenshots devote two navigation bars plus multiple full-height promotional rails to chrome; at 360 px the desktop canvas is clipped and adjacent cards remain visible off-screen.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise a compact mobile header and stack or snap content modules so the core task dominates each viewport.

findings.summary: Public templates omit the viewport meta tag and render a desktop canvas on phones.
findings.evidence: All home/search/product/cart DOM captures report hasViewportMeta=false. At 360x800 the homepage layout reports a 1000 px inner canvas and 640 px horizontal overflow; the screenshot shows clipped desktop navigation and cards.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a valid width=device-width viewport declaration and rebuild global/header/card layouts with intrinsic fluid sizing and narrow-screen reflow.

findings.summary: Reusable modules do not demonstrate component-level adaptation.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS probes found no @container rules, while the same catalogue and product modules remain desktop-sized in narrow captures.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce size containers and container queries for reused cards, nav modules and commerce panels.

findings.summary: Some controls are undersized or lose visible keyboard focus.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse target-size failed on two groups; the product focus probe counted 19 sub-24 px targets and showed several global links/buttons with outline:none after programmatic focus, including Add to basket shortcuts.
findings.suggestedFix: Ensure at least 24x24 CSS px targets with spacing and preserve a strong :focus-visible indicator on every interactive control.

findings.summary: Cold-load performance is poor.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse performance scored 0.37 with FCP 6.5 s, LCP 15.2 s, TBT 840 ms and TTI 19.1 s. The raw-CDP trace corroborated FCP 4.51 s, LCP 4.57 s and two long tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP dependency chain, prioritise the LCP asset, and break up/defer non-critical main-thread work.

findings.summary: The load ships a heavy blocking resource graph.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 127 requests and 2.89 MB transferred, including 1.06 MB script, 735 KB fonts, 10 grounded render-blocking candidates, and 2.43 MB from non-main origins; a WAF challenge script alone transferred 591 KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Shorten blocking CSS chains, subset/preload only critical fonts, defer scripts, and conditionally load non-critical dependencies.

findings.summary: Accessible names and ARIA semantics contain defects.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found aria-allowed-attr, aria-prohibited-attr and label-content-name-mismatch failures; image probes found 2 missing alts on home, 7 on search and 38 on product.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct role/ARIA combinations and accessible names; give meaningful images accurate alt and decorative images empty alt.

findings.summary: Keyboard and accessibility-tree quality is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports a malformed agent accessibility tree; focus probing showed multiple visible controls with no outline, and the consent Accept/Decline inputs computed outline:none.
findings.suggestedFix: Repair tree semantics and apply consistent :focus-visible styling without suppressing native outlines.

findings.summary: Zoom/reflow support is undermined by the missing viewport and small targets.
findings.evidence: Every representative DOM lacked viewport meta, narrow layouts retained 980–1000 px canvases, and Lighthouse failed target size.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a scalable viewport, reflow layouts at narrow widths, and enlarge/space touch targets.

findings.summary: The homepage logs browser errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse errors-in-console failed with one recorded error.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the underlying runtime/network error or handle the expected failure without emitting a console error.

findings.summary: Image and document asset hygiene is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found six incorrect-aspect-ratio instances; image probes found 41/42 home images and 89/100 product images without both dimensions. Doctype and UTF-8 charset pass.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio and avoid distorting responsive images.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and inspector hygiene failures remain.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse deprecations failed with two items; browser console errors also occurred.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace deprecated APIs and keep the page free of DevTools deprecation/console issues.

findings.summary: Search and basket templates omit essential metadata and indexing signals.
findings.evidence: DOM metadata summary shows search and cart have no meta description or canonical; search also has no structured/share metadata. Lighthouse reports one non-crawlable anchor.
findings.suggestedFix: Add unique descriptions and appropriate canonical/indexing signals to public templates and keep navigation anchors crawlable.

findings.summary: Product entities lack structured and social-preview metadata.
findings.evidence: Product probe found zero JSON-LD and zero Open Graph tags despite a visible named product, price, rating and availability.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit accurate schema.org Product/Offer JSON-LD plus Open Graph preview metadata matching visible content.

findings.summary: Core browser security headers and cookie protections are missing.
findings.evidence: HTTPS passes, but the headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy. Cookie audit found 7/8 cookies insecure and auth-like session-id/session-id-time not HttpOnly.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a tested CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; mark sensitive cookies Secure, HttpOnly and with the narrowest SameSite.

findings.summary: The first load has a broad third-party/data-processing footprint.
findings.evidence: Consent copy names 129 third parties. HAR attributes 112/127 requests and 2.43 MB to non-main origins, though the tracker primitive found no known third-party tracker domains and secrets scan found no credentials.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise pre-consent requests, audit each vendor/affiliate origin, and defer optional analytics or advertising until informed consent.

findings.summary: Homepage and search content collapse for non-JavaScript crawlers.
findings.evidence: Discoverability captures report homepage 1% raw/rendered word coverage (HTTP 202) and search 0%, both isJsShell=true; by contrast product content is 96% present, showing the resilient product pattern is achievable.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render meaningful homepage/search content and crawlable links, then progressively enhance interactivity.

findings.summary: No installable/offline product surface was exposed.
findings.evidence: Platform probe found an active service-worker controller but no manifest link; no installable identity or offline fallback was exposed on the commerce entry page.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a manifest and intentional offline/failure fallback for app-like shopping surfaces, or explicitly scope this capability out.

findings.summary: Image delivery is wasteful across key templates.
findings.evidence: Home uses 35 legacy images and 40 images without srcset; product uses 91 legacy images, 51 oversized images and 89 missing dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP where useful, right-size sources with srcset/sizes, reserve dimensions and lazy-load below-fold media.

findings.summary: Background and third-party work exceeds a proportionate first-load budget.
findings.evidence: HAR shows 127 requests/2.89 MB, 24 scripts/1.06 MB and 112 non-main-origin requests; Lighthouse TBT is 840 ms and TTI 19.1 s.
findings.suggestedFix: Set per-template budgets, conditionally load optional code, and deprioritise background fetch/analytics.

findings.summary: Agentic commerce capabilities are not exposed as structured tools.
findings.evidence: The public product/search flows are relevant to agents, but the platform probe found no WebMCP surface and Lighthouse found the agent accessibility tree malformed.
findings.suggestedFix: Pilot narrow, safe WebMCP tools or agentic forms for search, product facts and basket actions with explicit confirmation.

findings.summary: No page-owned on-device inference enhancement was observed.
findings.evidence: Chrome exposes LanguageModel and Summarizer globals in the probe, but the page registered no observable on-device summarisation or product-comparison capability.
findings.suggestedFix: Treat this as an opportunity: evaluate private on-device summarisation/comparison only where it improves the shopping task and has a non-AI fallback.

taskList.title: Restore true mobile reflow and target/focus usability
Reduce LCP, blocking code and first-load network cost
Harden response headers and cookie attributes
Fix ARIA, accessible names, focus and image alternatives
Reduce and semantically implement the consent interruption
Add dark, reduced-motion and forced-colour preference support
Minimise pre-consent and non-main-origin data flows
Progressively adopt declarative navigation and transitions
Reduce chrome density on primary surfaces
Add manifest and intentional offline fallback
